sent: Frank Zappa's influence on music is undeniable, and his work on Studio Tan is a testament to that. Released on the first day of 1978, this album showcases his versatility, blending jazz fusion with other styles. One notable piece from the album is The Adventures of Greggery Peccary, which stands out for its experimental rock elements. This track highlights Zappa's unique approach, pushing the boundaries of conventional genres and offering listeners a rich, eclectic experience.

The song Hate Me, a hallmark of alternative rock, was released on January 24, 2006, by the band Blue October. This track is part of their album Foiled, which came out a couple of months later on April 4, 2006. The album, produced by David Castell, features performances exclusively in English and was released under Universal Records. Blue October's distinct sound and compelling production define both the single and the album, cementing their place in the rock music scene of the early 2000s.

Released on December 11, 2009, and featuring the creative lyrics of Yanou, Welcome to the Club is a catchy tune performed by DJ Manian. It's a dynamic piece, firmly rooted in the electronic dance music genre, and delivered in English, inviting listeners around the world to join in its energetic rhythms.

Mark Knopfler, known for his distinctive baritone voice, both composed and wrote the lyrics for Walk of Life, a lively track that blends rock music with elements of country rock. Released at the start of 1985, this catchy tune is performed by the iconic band Dire Straits and is sung in English. It finds its place among other classic hits on the Brothers in Arms album, contributing to the record's acclaim and enduring popularity.

In 1963, Boots Randolph released the lively and humorous tune Yakety Sax, showcasing his dual talents as both its composer and performer. Famously associated with comedic chase scenes, this saxophone-driven piece remains one of Randolph's signature works. Despite its lighthearted tone, the song has stood the test of time, highlighting Randolph's skillful musical craftsmanship.

Back to Black, widely recognized as one of Amy Winehouse's standout albums, features the track Just Friends, which Winehouse herself both composed and performed. This jazz piece, expressing an authentic emotional intensity, is delivered in her signature contralto voice that resonates with listeners. Within the album, Just Friends is one of the tracks that showcases her lyrical prowess and deep connection to the genre she adored, further cementing her legacy in the world of music.

Here I Go Again, performed by Whitesnake, is one of the standout tracks from their album Saints & Sinners. Released on November 15, 1982, this song quickly captured the attention of rock enthusiasts and showcased the band's signature sound. The album, under the Geffen Records label, holds a special place in the music world, with Here I Go Again remaining a fan favorite for decades.

Cantata misericordium, composed by the renowned Benjamin Britten, first saw the light of day as a published work on January 1, 1963. This piece, crafted in the timeless Latin language, adds to Britten's remarkable repertoire, showcasing his unique ability to blend traditional elements with his innovative style.

Afrika, known for their unique sound and vibrant performances, is elegantly brought to life by the talented KFT. Their collaboration infuses the piece with energy that captivates audiences, showcasing a dynamic musical synergy.

Crafted by Friedrich Wille, the Hauptsatzkantate takes the listener on a journey through its evocative German lyrics. This musical piece was introduced to the world at the start of 1984, marking an important addition to the era's classical compositions.

Released at the dawn of 1959, Blue in Green stands as a quintessential piece in the jazz genre. The composition carries the distinctive marks of both Miles Davis and Bill Evans, who interestingly share the credit for composing this timeless tune. Although it's Davis who is primarily known for performing the piece, Evans' influence is undeniably woven into its haunting melodies and introspective mood.

Through the Looking Glass, an album performed by Siouxsie and the Banshees, offers an eclectic blend of post-punk and alternative rock. Released by Polydor Records, this album includes, among its tracks, the song The Passenger. Mike Hedges, with his production expertise, has certainly added a unique touch to this notable work.

György Ligeti, known for his innovative compositions, created Musica ricercata which showcases his unique style through the piano. This piece highlights the instrument's versatility, bringing Ligeti's artistic vision to life through intricate melodies and rhythms.

Loco in Acapulco, composed by the versatile Phil Collins, is a rhythm and blues piece that takes listeners back to the vibrant musical landscape of the late '80s. Released at the very start of 1988, this track captures the essence of that era with its infectious beats and soulful vibe. Collins' expertise in crafting melodies truly shines through this memorable work.

Lindsay Lohan's track Over is a notable piece from her album Speak, perfectly capturing the essence of the early 2000s pop scene. Released at the very start of 2004, it stands out not only as one of the prominent tracks from the album alongside Rumors but also as a collaboration between Lohan and other talented artists. The song's composition is credited to Kara DioGuardi, while the lyrics are crafted by Lohan herself, along with John Shanks and DioGuardi, all contributing to its engaging vibe. The vocals are delivered in English, adding to its widespread appeal.

Better Man is part of the album Sing When You're Winning, which is a notable work of pop music produced by Guy Chambers. Released on August 28, 2000, this album features tracks in English and showcases a vibrant blend of melodic tunes and catchy lyrics.

Solar Music made its debut on the music scene at the very beginning of 1974. This work, introduced during an era that witnessed significant shifts in musical expression, continues to resonate through the decades with its unique sound.

Ralph Vaughan Williams composed Symphony No. 8, which first emerged into the world on January 1, 1955. This piece is a testament to his unique style, revealing the profound insights he had into musical expression during the mid-20th century.

Released under Columbia Records, Shakira's album Pies Descalzos features several captivating tracks. Among these is Un poco de amor, a song that not only highlights the artist's signature style but also showcases her lyrical prowess, as she penned the lyrics herself. This Spanish-language track, alongside others like Estoy Aquí and Antología, is part of the eclectic mix that defines the album. With these compositions, Shakira truly made her mark in the music world.

The Bonnie Blue Flag is an interesting piece composed by Harry McCarthy, who also performed it. This song made its first appearance at the start of 1861 and is rendered in English. It's fascinating to think about how the same person who composed this work also brought it to life through his performances.

The album Feuer und Flamme, performed by Nena, is a notable piece in the pop music genre. Among its tracks, Haus der drei Sonnen stands out, sharing the same musical style. While both songs are quintessentially German, the lyrical contribution of Uwe Fahrenkrog-Petersen on Haus der drei Sonnen adds a distinct flavor to the piece within the album. These elements come together to create a cohesive and captivating musical experience.

Franz Schubert, a prolific composer, completed his Symphony No. 9, which was published on January 1, 1839, adding a significant piece to the Romantic repertoire. This symphony, often celebrated for its grandeur and expressive depth, stands as a testament to Schubert's mastery in orchestration and melodic development. Despite his passing over a decade before its publication, Schubert's influence on classical music endured, and this symphony remains a beloved work in orchestral performances worldwide.

Kol Nidrei, a composition by Max Bruch, made its debut at the dawn of 1881. This evocative piece features a prominent cello, harmoniously accompanied by a string orchestra. Its rich instrumentation allows the work to resonate with depth and emotion, capturing listeners' hearts since its introduction.
Richard Strauss composed Death and Transfiguration, a symphonic poem that debuted at the start of 1890. Scored for a full orchestra, this work captures profound themes and is a standout in the genre.

Don't Let the Sun Go Down on Me, composed by the legendary Elton John, made its debut at the very start of 1974. This iconic piece, which features lyrics penned by Bernie Taupin, resonates beautifully in English. The collaboration between John and Taupin once again delivered a song that has captured the hearts of many over the years.

Released in English on the first day of 1984, this song is part of their album Love at First Sting, which followed later that year in March. Recorded under the EMI label, this album, like the single, is delivered in English and has cemented its place as a classic within the genre.

The classic Christmas tune Have Yourself a Merry Little Christmas, crafted in the English language by composers and lyricists Hugh Martin and Ralph Blane, first graced the public's ears on January 1, 1943. Known for its soothing melody and festive charm, this beloved piece of Christmas music has been beautifully performed by the iconic Judy Garland, whose rich contralto voice added a distinctive warmth to the song.

Take My Breath Away, sung in English, quickly became iconic, solidifying its place in the musical landscape not just for its association with the film, but also for its mesmerizing melody and heartfelt performance.

sent: Claude Debussy, the brilliant composer, crafted the enchanting work known as Préludes, which he published at the start of 1912. Designed for solo piano, this collection showcases Debussy's innovative use of the instrument. Its distinct sound and intricate compositions have left a lasting mark in the world of music, brilliantly illustrating his mastery and creativity.

Back in the early '60s, surf music was making waves, and one song that stood out was Hawaii Tattoo. Released at the start of 1961, this track was performed by The Waikikis, who captured the essence of the genre perfectly. Their interpretation brought the vibrant and laid-back vibes of surf culture to life, becoming a hallmark of that musical era.

The iconic album The Wall, released on November 30, 1979, by the renowned record label Harvest, features a number of remarkable tracks including Goodbye Cruel World and Young Lust. Pink Floyd, the legendary band, brings the English-language lyrics penned by Roger Waters to life in Goodbye Cruel World, a track that forms part of this conceptual masterpiece. The album itself is part of the larger work, Shine On, showcasing a cohesive yet diverse exploration of themes through its impressive lineup.

The song Oerend Hard, performed by the band Normaal, is a classic piece of dialect music that first reached audiences on April 30, 1977. Sung in Achterhooks, the track captures the essence of regional sounds and storytelling.

Nikolai Myaskovsky, a distinguished composer, crafted Symphony No. 25, which made its debut at the start of 1946. This work reflects the unique style and depth that Myaskovsky is celebrated for, capturing listeners with its intricate harmonies and profound emotional depth. Symphony No. 25, emerging shortly after the tumultuous events of the early 20th century, remains a significant piece in the classical music repertoire, illustrating Myaskovsky's exceptional talent and the enduring power of his compositions.

The St. Cecilia Mass, composed by Charles Gounod, first made its appearance to the public in 1855. This magnificent choral work quickly showcased Gounod's exceptional talent, cementing his reputation in the realm of sacred music.

Solid, a soulful track written by the talented duo Nickolas Ashford and Valerie Simpson, was brought to the public’s ears at the start of 1984. Both Ashford and Simpson not only composed but also penned the lyrics, crafting them in English. This classic piece was performed by the pair themselves, famously known as Ashford & Simpson, marking their artistry in the music industry.

Solidaritätslied, published on January 1, 1930, is a compelling piece that falls under the genre of industrial folk music. This work, with its unique blend of traditional folk elements and the raw aesthetics of industrial sound, captures the essence of a time when music served as a powerful medium for social and political commentary.

Ixnay on the Hombre, produced by Dave Jerden and released by Epitaph Records on February 4, 1997, includes the skate punk track The Meaning of Life. Written by Dexter Holland, this song captures the energetic and rebellious spirit characteristic of the genre. Although it is part of the album released earlier in the year, The Meaning of Life came out later on August 15, 1997, adding an extra layer of depth to the already dynamic collection.

Released on January 1, 1971, Heart of Gold is a classic example of Neil Young's songwriting prowess. While he composed and penned the lyrics himself, the song stands out as an enduring piece in the English language. Its timeless appeal continues to resonate with audiences, showcasing Young's unique ability to craft melodies that linger in the heart.

Heckerlied, a piece steeped deeply in its historical context, emerged on the first day of the year 1848. It carries the lyrical touch of Friedrich Hecker, reflecting the fervor and tumult of its time. Written in German, the song embodies the spirit and struggles encapsulated in its verses.

The musical work, with its compelling lyrics crafted by Roger Waters, takes listeners on a unique auditory journey. David Gilmour's contribution as the composer ensures that this track maintains its distinct and memorable sound, highlighting the band's creativity and expressive prowess.

Arnold Schoenberg's brilliance shines through in his composition Pelleas und Melisande, a work that reflects his unique approach to orchestration and thematic development. The piece showcases his ability to weave intricate melodies and harmonies, capturing listeners with its emotional depth and complexity. Schoenberg's influence on modern music is evident in this compelling composition, which continues to resonate with audiences today.

Released on August 24, 1981, Tattoo You is an English-language hard rock album that showcases the talents of its creators. Under the banners of Universal Music Group and Virgin Records, this album features tracks like Heaven and Little T&A. Among its notable songs, Start Me Up stands out as a distinctive piece that exemplifies the genre's energy and vigor.

Rick Astley, known for his distinctive lyric baritone voice, brings his unique sound to Ain't Too Proud to Beg. His vocal style adds a fresh twist to the song, making it a memorable rendition in his live performances.

Mozart's Flute Concerto No. 1 beautifully showcases the interplay between the flute and the orchestra. This composition, crafted by the genius of Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart, captivates audiences with its elegant dialogue between the solo instrument and the accompanying ensemble. The concerto remains a timeless piece in the classical flute repertoire, demonstrating Mozart's extraordinary talent in writing for both solo instruments and orchestral arrangements.

It's the Same Old Song is a classic soul piece, a testament to the collaborative genius of Brian Holland, Eddie Holland, and Lamont Dozier. This English-language tune not only showcases their skills as composers but also highlights their lyrical talents. With its engaging melody and heartfelt lyrics, the song captures the essence of soul music, drawing listeners in with each note.

Carl Czerny, well-known for his contributions to piano repertoire, composed the work titled School of Velocity. This collection of pieces is specifically crafted for piano, showcasing his mastery in writing for the instrument. Through it, he aimed to enhance the pianist's technical prowess and agility on the keys.

Robert Schumann's Humoreske is a delightful piece for the piano that exemplifies the humoresque genre. Crafted with Schumann's distinctive emotional depth, this work invites pianists to explore its rich and whimsical character. Through this composition, Schumann offers a charming blend of humor and introspection, providing a captivating experience for both the performer and the listener.

Back in the mid-80s, Roxette brought us the catchy pop tune Neverending Love, with Per Gessle at the helm as both composer and lyricist. Released as part of the Pearls of Passion album, this English-language track fit snugly within the pop music genre that was all the rage at the time. It found its home under the EMI label, which helped spread the duo's fame.

David Bowie, known for his distinctive baritone voice, composed Moonage Daydream, a song that showcases his unique style. In this piece, not only did he leave his mark through its composition, but he also performed it himself, bringing his powerful voice to the forefront. Sharing the stage with him were The Arnold Corns, who also contributed their talents to the rendition of this iconic track. This collaboration is a testament to Bowie's versatility and influence in the music world.

The song Ain't Nobody, crafted by the talented composers Dallas Austin, Treach, and Dale Warren, first saw the light of day on January 1, 1995. Its English lyrics were penned by both Dallas Austin and Treach, showcasing their creative synergy.

Roger Cicero brought his unique flair and vocal prowess to the song Frauen regier'n die Welt. His performance of the piece captures its vibrant and lively spirit, showcasing his ability to engage and enthrall an audience with his charming stage presence and emotive delivery.

Sonny Boy comes to life through the creative collaboration of its talented composers, Buddy DeSylva, Ray Henderson, and Al Jolson. This classic piece is delivered in English and carries heartfelt lyrics crafted by Ray Henderson and Lew Brown. The blend of their musical and lyrical prowess gives this song its timeless charm.

Igor Stravinsky composed Le roi des étoiles, a captivating piece that made its public debut in early 1912. This work, like much of Stravinsky's music, is a testament to his innovative style and profound impact on the world of classical music during that era.

The haunting track Lacrymosa, known for its symphonic metal flair, showcases the powerful mezzo-soprano voice of Amy Lee. This captivating piece is performed by Evanescence and is part of their 2006 album, The Open Door. In addition to Lacrymosa, the album features other notable songs such as Weight of the World, Sweet Sacrifice, Call Me When You're Sober, and Cloud Nine. These tracks together highlight the band's dynamic range and artistic depth.

She Is Love is a charming alternative rock track composed and written by Noel Gallagher. Released on January 1, 2002, it stands out as part of the Heathen Chemistry album. Oasis brings this song to life with their distinctive style, adding to the album's Britpop essence. In addition to this track, fans will find Hung in a Bad Place and Little by Little among the collection's offerings, each contributing to the album's memorable soundscape.

Max Martin composed the pop track Let There Be Love, which features Christina Aguilera as the performer. Released on the first day of 2012, the song is part of the album Lotus. This album, known for its popular music style, also includes tracks like Army of Me and Lotus Intro. Alex da Kid lent his expertise as the producer, helping to craft the sound under the RCA Records label. With Aguilera's powerful vocals showcased throughout, the English-language project stands as a notable entry in her discography.

Orion, a noteworthy piece in the thrash metal genre, showcases the collaborative genius of Cliff Burton and James Hetfield. While Burton composed the music, Hetfield penned the evocative lyrics, further enriching the song with the deep, resonant tone of his baritone voice. This successful combination of composition and lyricism marks Orion as a standout in its musical category.

Eddie Vedder, known for his powerful voice and emotive songwriting, composed Porch, a notable track from the acclaimed album Ten. This album, a cornerstone of alternative rock, not only features Porch but also includes other memorable tracks like Oceans and Why Go. Together, these songs create a dynamic and immersive listening experience that has captivated audiences for decades.

Carl Maria von Weber composed Invitation to the Dance, a delightful piece arranged for piano. This composition exemplifies Weber's genius and has captured the imagination of listeners with its elegant charm and musical storytelling, all expressed through the nuances of the piano.

Sergei Prokofiev's talent truly shines in his Piano Sonata No. 8, a masterpiece he crafted in the mid-20th century. This powerful piece, completed in early 1944, showcases the piano's expressive range and Prokofiev's innovative style. The sonata reflects the unique musical landscape of the era, affirming its place in the repertoire of classical pianists worldwide.

In 1969, the progressive rock masterpiece The Court of the Crimson King was brought to life by the talented composer Ian McDonald, with evocative lyrics penned by Peter Sinfield. This song, sung in English, is just one stunning piece from the album In the Court of the Crimson King, released on October 10th of that year. The entire album, performed by the iconic band King Crimson and released under Island Records, showcases the genre of popular music at its best. Known for its imaginative and intricate sound, it remains a landmark in music history.

La golondrina, a piece crafted by the talented Narciso Serradell Sevilla, has found a place in the repertoires of numerous celebrated artists. Among those who have brought this evocative music to life are the versatile singer-songwriter Caetano Veloso, the multi-talented entertainer Caterina Valente, and the renowned tenor Plácido Domingo. Each performer adds their unique touch to the composition, showcasing its timeless appeal and emotional depth.
Frank Bridge, a notable composer, crafted the piece Threads (Two intermezzi). This work, which reflects his unique style, was published at the start of 1921.

Peder Gram's Symphony No. 3, which was composed by him, saw its publication on the first day of 1954. This piece represents a significant work in Gram's repertoire and contributes to the rich tapestry of mid-20th-century classical music.

The song Hunting High and Low has a powerful and emotional feel, thanks to the combined talents of its creators. Crafted by the talented Paul Waaktaar-Savoy, who not only composed the piece but also penned its lyrics, it carries a unique signature. The iconic band a-ha brings the track to life, with their performance capturing the depth and nuance intended by its composer and lyricist.

Franz Liszt, the renowned composer, poured his creativity into the piece Années de pèlerinage, which he structured to be performed on the piano. This work captures the essence of Liszt's virtuosity and is celebrated for its challenging yet evocative composition, showcasing both technical brilliance and emotional depth through the instrument's rich tonal possibilities.

Ennio Morricone, the renowned composer and performer, gave the world Chi Mai in early 1971. This piece, synonymous with his name, highlights Morricone's profound ability to evoke emotion through music. Chi Mai's enduring appeal and the timeless quality reflect Morricone's mastery in composition and performance.

U2's album The Joshua Tree features an array of iconic rock tracks. Among them, One Tree Hill stands out not only for its place on this legendary album but also for its poignant rock vibe, delivered in English. Alongside it, fans can find other classics like With or Without You and Red Hill Mining Town, showcasing the band's profound impact on the genre. Each song contributes to the album's enduring legacy in rock music.

The Weerbaarhedenlied is a song with lyrics written in Dutch. This piece captures the essence of its cultural and linguistic roots, resonating with speakers of the language and those familiar with its thematic nuances.

Worried Life Blues, performed by Big Maceo Merriweather, is a classic piece rooted in the blues genre. Released on January 1, 1941, this English-language song captures the emotive depth and soulful essence characteristic of its time. Merriweather's delivery remains a quintessential example of the blues' ability to convey profound emotion through its stirring melodies and poignant lyrics.

La Mer, a quintessential French chanson, was brought to life by Charles Trenet and Albert Lasry, who composed its timeless melody with Trenet also penning the evocative lyrics. The album itself, produced by Bob Ezrin, delves into progressive rock and includes tracks like Outside the Wall, all infused with the creative sound by the band in the English language.

Trade Winds, composed by Natasha Barrett, made its debut at the start of 2008. Released on New Year's Day in 2008, this composition has continued to resonate with listeners ever since.

The song Constantly, written by Saverio Seracini with lyrics crafted by Vincenzo D'Acquisto, was brought to life in the English language by performer Cliff Richard. Released to the public on the first day of 1963, this piece showcases the collaboration of these talented individuals.

Alfred Schnittke, a renowned composer, created the musical work Nagasaki, which was published at the beginning of 1958. This piece reflects the profound impact and themes surrounding its namesake, showcasing Schnittke's ability to convey deep emotion through his music.

In the realm of pop music, the English language tune You Like Me Too Much stands out as a work both composed and penned by George Harrison. Released on the first day of 1965, this song features the iconic performance of The Beatles, adding another gem to their illustrious discography.

Senhora do Mar (Negras Águas) is a captivating piece performed by Vânia Fernandes that perfectly embodies the essence of fado, a genre steeped in emotion and tradition. This song, delivered in the beautiful Portuguese language, envelops listeners with its haunting melodies and rich cultural heritage, making it a standout performance in Fernandes' repertoire.

Heitor Villa-Lobos composed the beautiful piece Canções de Cordialidade, which features the expressive sound of the piano. This composition showcases the Brazilian composer’s ability to blend intricate melodies with the rich tones of the instrument, making it a remarkable addition to any pianistic repertoire.

The song Black Hole Sun, composed by Chris Cornell, is a notable track from Soundgarden's album Superunknown. Released on the first day of 1994, it quickly became a hallmark of 90s rock music. This piece is delivered in English and features Cornell's distinctive vocal style, contributing to its lasting appeal and recognition.

Ned Rorem, a renowned composer, gifted the world his Double Concerto on the first day of 1998. This captivating piece, showcasing Rorem's distinctive style and craftsmanship, quickly found its place in the hearts of classical music enthusiasts.

Heitor Villa-Lobos, the renowned Brazilian composer, crafted the remarkable piece known as String Quartet No. 13. His unique style weaves cultural influences into his compositions, and this quartet is no exception, showcasing his distinctive blend of rich harmonies and rhythmic innovation.

This lively English track features the engaging vocals of AnnaSophia Robb, whose performance brings a unique charm to the song. The piece's message and melody continue to resonate with listeners who appreciate its heartfelt delivery.

The iconic song Live and Let Die showcases the talents of Paul and Linda McCartney, who both composed and penned its lyrics. Released at the start of 1973, this popular music piece was brought to life by the band Wings, with Paul McCartney's tenor voice contributing significantly to its distinct sound. Johann Sebastian Bach, one of the most influential composers of the Baroque era, crafted the cantata Herr Jesu Christ, wahr' Mensch und Gott, BWV 127. Lost in Love is an English-language soft rock piece that gained attention when it was performed by both Stephanie Ho and Air Supply. Franz Schubert crafted a masterpiece with his String Quartet No. 13, a work that showcases his exceptional talent and deep emotional range. This quartet, with its rich harmonies and evocative melodies, stands as a testament to Schubert's genius and continues to captivate listeners even today.

Joseph Haydn, the renowned composer, crafted Symphony No. 19 as one of his early works. This piece adds to the rich tapestry of his extensive symphonic output, showcasing his developing style and musical ideas.

In the world of French chanson, La Belle amour holds a special place. Richard Strauss composed Burleske, a captivating piece that brings the piano and orchestra together in a lively dance. The interplay between the solo piano and the orchestral accompaniment creates a dynamic and engaging atmosphere, showcasing Strauss's mastery at blending these musical forces seamlessly.

Genesis, known for their contributions to progressive rock, released the album Foxtrot under both Virgin Records and Atlantic Records. This album features compelling tracks such as Watcher of the Skies and Get 'Em Out by Friday, showcasing the band's signature style. As a part of the progressive rock genre, Foxtrot stands as a testament to Genesis's innovative approach to music during that era.

Back in the early 20th century, Alexander von Zemlinsky composed the evocative work Die Seejungfrau. Released on the first day of January in 1903, this piece reflects Zemlinsky's distinctive style and remains a notable example of his contributions to classical music.

Released on the first day of 1994, Hakuna Matata is a catchy tune that has charmed audiences with its infectious rhythm and joyful spirit. Composed by the legendary Elton John, this song seamlessly blends the essence of show tunes with elements of popular music. It's performed by a talented group, including Lebo M., Joseph Williams, and Nathan Lane, who bring the English-language track to life with their vibrant performances.

Released on November 16, 2012, Unheilig performed this captivating piece, Stark, which falls within the pop music genre. The lyrics, crafted by Der Graf, infuse the song with their unique artistry, making it a memorable addition to their repertoire.

John Barleycorn is a folk song that has been passed down through generations, and it beautifully captures the essence of English storytelling through music. Its lyrics weave a narrative that resonates with the cultural heritage of England, showcasing the richness of the language within its verses.

The evocative composition Le jeune homme et la mort was crafted by the masterful Johann Sebastian Bach. This work, with its intricate melodies and profound themes, showcases Bach’s unparalleled ability to weave complex musical narratives. His talent shines through the piece, leaving listeners entranced by its depth and emotional range.

triples.sub: Le jeune homme et la mort

sent: Justin Timberlake, collaborating with Scott Storch, crafted the emotional ballad Cry Me a River as part of his hit album Justified. It's a standout track where Timberlake's vocals beautifully express heartache. This album—anchored by the compelling storytelling and intricate composition of Cry Me a River—was recognized on a broader scale, earning a nomination for the American Music Award for Favorite Pop/Rock Album.

triples.obj: American Music Award for Favorite Pop/Rock Album

sent: Robert Schumann, the brilliant composer, crafted a piece called Toccata specifically for the piano. This work, with its intricate and energetic melodies, first found its way to the public in January of 1834. Schumann's Toccata is a notable example of his talent and ability to push the piano's boundaries, reflecting both the technical prowess required and his deep understanding of the instrument.

Released at the start of 2006, Who Says You Can't Go Home is a heartland rock track performed by Bon Jovi. This song is featured on their album Have a Nice Day. Island Records, known for its roster of influential artists, handled the album’s production. Bon Jovi's powerful vocals and spirited energy are evident in both this track and the album as a whole.

sent: Georges Bizet, a renowned composer, crafted the delightful musical work Jeux d'enfants. This charming piece is particularly notable for its instrumentation, designed for piano four hands. It's a playful and engaging suite that captures the whimsical spirit associated with childhood games, showcasing Bizet's ability to create vivid imagery through music.
Ye Sacred Muses was crafted by the renowned composer William Byrd, who infused it with his signature style. Byrd's work stands as a testament to his expertise and lasting influence on choral music.

Stars is an iconic rock song that's part of the album Hear 'n Aid – An All-Star Album for Famine Relief. This powerful track, written by Jimmy Bain, contributes to the album's mission to aid famine relief through its compelling lyrics. The entire album is performed in English, ensuring its message reaches a wide audience.

triples.obj: Hear 'n Aid – An All-Star Album for Famine Relief

sent: Longplayer, composed by Jem Finer, made its debut at the turn of the millennium. Released on January 1, 2000, this unique musical piece stands out for its innovative concept and execution.

Luigi Nono's composition, Hay que caminar, emerged at the dawn of 1989, marking a significant moment in modern music. This piece showcases Nono’s distinct style and innovative approach, which has been captivating audiences since its release.

Released on October 1, 1968, The Book of Taliesyn showcases Deep Purple's prowess in the hard rock genre. This album, performed by the legendary band and produced by Derek Lawrence, was brought to the public by both Tetragrammaton Records and Harvest. Among its captivating tracklist is the song Anthem, with lyrics penned by Rod Evans. Deep Purple's impressive work on this English-language album includes other notable tracks like Listen, Learn, Read On, solidifying their presence in rock music history.

Rostige Flügel, a compelling piece of country rock, first caught the public's attention when it was released on the first of September in 1984. The music delivers the evocative sounds typical of the genre, drawing listeners into its rustic charm and evocative storytelling.
Glen Vella brought his vibrant energy to the track One Life, which debuted in 2011. The piece captures the essence of that year, as Vella's spirited performance continues to resonate with audiences.

Leroy Anderson is well-known for his delightful piece Sleigh Ride, a charming example of light music. First performed on January 1, 1948, this vibrant composition captures the festive spirit perfectly. The Boston Pops Orchestra, with their skillful and spirited rendition, brought this wintry classic to audiences, making it an enduring favorite during the holiday season.

Martin Gore, known for his tenor voice and lyrical contributions, composed the synth-pop piece Home. This track, performed in English, finds its place among other notable songs on the album Ultra. Fans of the genre can also appreciate Insight, another track from the same album, showcasing Gore's distinctive style and musical influence.

Achtung Baby, an essential piece of alternative rock, was released under Island Records and includes tracks like The Fly, One, and Love Is Blindness. The latter, performed by the iconic band U2, made its debut at the start of 1991 and became a notable component of this celebrated album. With its rich tracklist and innovative sound, Achtung Baby not only captivated audiences but also earned a nomination for a Grammy Award for Album of the Year.

triples.obj: Grammy Award for Album of the Year

sent: Back in the early 2000s, Pink burst onto the music scene with Get the Party Started, a song that set the tone for her debut album, Missundaztood. Released on October 9, 2001, and penned by the talented Linda Perry, this track quickly became a hit. Missundaztood, which features a blend of pop and rock music, further solidified Pink's place in the industry when it was released on November 20, 2001. Linda Perry not only wrote Get the Party Started but also lent her production skills to the album, helping Pink create an eclectic and memorable collection of songs that are still celebrated today.

Pink Floyd's iconic album The Wall, released on November 30, 1979, is a cornerstone of progressive rock and showcases the band's innovative sound. This masterpiece, produced by Bob Ezrin and released under the Harvest label, features a range of memorable tracks, including Young Lust. Within this larger work is the compelling piece The Trial, also a product of Ezrin's musical genius, contributing significantly to the album's narrative. Part of the overarching concept is explored through Shine On, another integral component of this ambitious album which highlights Pink Floyd's artistry and versatility.
John Adams composed On the Transmigration of Souls, which was released at the start of 2002. This powerful piece is known for its emotional depth and artistic complexity.

All Blues, a legendary piece composed and performed by the iconic jazz musician Miles Davis, made its debut in the world on January 1, 1959. This timeless track, rooted in the rich traditions of jazz, continues to captivate listeners with its soulful melody and intricate rhythms. It's a testament to Davis’s exceptional talent and his lasting impact on the music scene.

Released on January 1, 2004, Miracle Drug is a rock music track by the iconic band U2. It is part of their album How to Dismantle an Atomic Bomb, which explores the pop rock genre. The album was introduced to the world under the aegis of Island Records, showcasing U2's versatility and depth in this album.

Released on October 5, 1942, this enchanting piece of traditional pop continues to captivate listeners with its English lyrics. Among the many performers who have brought life to the song is Janet Blair, whose rendition adds a magical touch to Porter's work.

sent: The album Over-Nite Sensation, a remarkable blend of progressive rock, funk rock, hard rock, and jazz fusion, showcases its diversity through tracks like the iconic Montana. Another standout piece from this album is Camarillo Brillo, which also embraces the progressive rock genre. This eclectic mix highlights the album’s unique sound that combines several musical styles, making it a fascinating listen for any rock enthusiast.

Alapalooza, released at the start of 1993, showcases "Weird Al" Yankovic's flair in English with its hard rock genre. It was produced under Scotti Bros. Records and features the song Jurassic Park. This particular track, which came out later that same year in October, exemplifies Yankovic's comedic rock style, demonstrating his unique talent for blending humor and music seamlessly.

The album Fresh Cream showcases the talents of the band Cream, with Robert Stigwood behind its production. Among the standout tracks on this album, "I'm So Glad" offers listeners a vibrant taste of their musical prowess.

Jim Steinman composed the popular music hit I'd Do Anything for Love (But I Won't Do That), which was released in the English language on September 15, 1993. This powerful ballad captivated audiences with its dramatic flair and heartfelt lyrics, showcasing Steinman's signature style.

sent: Because the Night is a song steeped in collaboration and musical legacy. Composed by both Bruce Springsteen and Patti Smith, it features lyrics penned by this iconic pair, showcasing their deep lyrical prowess. Initially brought to life by the Patti Smith Group, the track later gained popularity with a cover by 10,000 Maniacs. Sung in English, the song is part of the album Easter, adding another layer to its significance in rock history.

Trem das Onze, a samba classic, was brought to the world by the talented Adoniran Barbosa. Released in early 1964, this piece quickly became emblematic of its genre. It's a delightful song performed and composed by Barbosa himself, with its lively rhythm and lyrics written in Portuguese capturing the authentic essence of Brazilian culture.

Danse visionaire, a captivating piece composed by Johan Halvorsen, made its debut at the start of 1898. This enchanting work was designed for both piano and violin, showcasing Halvorsen's talent in blending these instruments. The piece has intrigued audiences ever since its original publication, drawing listeners into its emotive and visionary musical landscape.

Here Comes Santa Claus (Right Down Santa Claus Lane), a festive tune often heard during the holidays, showcases the collaborative talents of Oakley Haldeman, who composed the piece and contributed to its lyrics alongside Gene Autry. Autry also brought the song to life with his performance, giving it its initial charm. Later, the iconic Elvis Presley added his own flair to the English-language Christmas classic, cementing its popularity.

sent: Billy Ocean, a prominent figure in the pop rock genre, made waves with his 1986 album Love Zone, produced by Wayne Brathwaite. Among the standout tracks is There'll Be Sad Songs, which showcases a soulful side while still fitting seamlessly into the album's overall feel. Both the album and the track feature English lyrics, highlighting Ocean's versatility and appeal across different musical styles.

The soul classic Reach Out I'll Be There was brought to life by the legendary Four Tops, who infused their passion into every note. This powerful anthem, written and composed by the talented trio of Brian Holland, Eddie Holland, and Lamont Dozier, first resonated with audiences in 1966. Sung in English, the song captures the essence of its genre, with lyrics and melody intricately woven by its creators, leaving a lasting impact on generations of music lovers.

The Who's performance of Overture showcases the rock anthem's origins with Pete Townshend, a talented tenor, as its composer. Released in early 1969, this piece is a sterling example of rock music from that era. Townshend's voice adds a distinct and memorable quality to the composition, capturing the spirit of its time.

Michael Jackson, known for his distinctive tenor voice, not only performed the song Best of Joy but also penned its lyrics. This track showcases his vocal range and lyrical talent, capturing the essence of his musical style.

Oh! Susanna is a quintessential piece of American folk music, both composed and performed by Stephen Foster. The song's lyrics, also penned by Foster, were introduced to the world on February 25, 1848. This English-language classic has become a staple in the folk genre, showcasing Foster's unique talent and enduring influence on American music history.

The track Rock 'n' Roll Star, performed by Oasis, is featured on their debut album, Definitely Maybe. Released on August 29, 1994, this album played a significant role in defining the Britpop genre of the time. Authored in English and produced by the band itself, Definitely Maybe was brought to life under the Creation Records label.

Anthropology, a bebop composition that debuted on January 1, 1945, showcases the collaborative genius of Dizzy Gillespie and Charlie Parker. This vibrant piece not only highlights their skills as composers but also exemplifies Parker's prowess as a performer. Its intricate rhythm and lively improvisation capture the essence of the bebop genre, forever securing its place in jazz history.

Shir LaShalom, composed by Yair Rosenblum with lyrics by Yaakov Rotblit, is a Hebrew protest song that first saw the light of day in early 1969. Known for its poignant message, the song has been performed by Rotblit himself, capturing the spirit of its era. As a significant piece in the genre of protest songs, it remains a powerful commentary on the pursuit of peace.

The song "Don't Bother Me" was composed by George Harrison and first made its appearance in the music scene at the start of 1963. Sung in English, it marked an early contribution by Harrison, adding to the rich tapestry of the era's musical offerings.

David Gilmour, with his distinct baritone voice, both composed and penned the lyrics for Fat Old Sun. This piece, performed by the iconic band Pink Floyd, beautifully blends elements of progressive rock, psychedelic folk, and progressive folk. Released in early October of 1970, the song showcases the rich tapestry of genres that characterized the era’s music scene.

The lively and elegant Künstlerleben, a masterpiece in the world of classical waltzes, is a testament to the genius of Johann Strauss II. This iconic piece, which translates to "Artist's Life," perfectly captures Strauss's ability to blend rhythm and melody, ensuring its place in concert halls and hearts worldwide. When listening to it, you can truly sense the vitality and charm that only Strauss could infuse into his compositions, marking it as a cornerstone of his celebrated repertoire.

The album The Unforgettable Fire, released under Island Records, features the song Bad, which stands out as one of its notable tracks. Bono, renowned for his powerful and evocative songwriting, penned the lyrics for the entire album, adding depth and emotion that resonate throughout each song.

Alan's Psychedelic Breakfast, a progressive rock piece released in early October 1970, is a unique composition by Roger Waters. The song, which features lyrics by David Gilmour, is performed in English. Its innovative style is characteristic of the era's experimental music scene.

Krzysztof Penderecki's Prelude for Clarinet, composed in the late 20th century, specifically in 1987, showcases his unique style and innovative use of the clarinet. This piece brings out the expressive potential of the instrument, highlighting Penderecki's skill as a composer.

Roger Waters, known for his baritone voice, composed and wrote the lyrics for Vera, an art rock piece performed by Pink Floyd. This song, sung in English, is part of the iconic progressive rock album The Wall, which was released on January 1, 1979. The Wall, an influential release from Columbia Records, includes other memorable tracks like Young Lust and In the Flesh?

Albert Schlippenbach composed Ein Heller und ein Batzen, a piece that has been resonating with audiences since it was first published on January 1, 1850. This work is a testament to Schlippenbach’s creative prowess during the mid-19th century.

The Piano Sonatas by Mosolov, crafted by the talented composer Alexander Mosolov, made their debut at the start of 1929. This collection, written for solo piano, showcases Mosolov's innovative approach to the instrument and reflects the musical avant-garde of its time. Though initially underappreciated, these sonatas gradually found recognition for their unique place in the early 20th-century repertoire, highlighting the intricate and bold compositions that Mosolov introduced to the world.

Stone Cold Crazy is a heavy metal track with a punchy and energetic vibe that showcases the collaborative genius of Freddie Mercury and Brian May, who both contributed as composers. The song's gripping lyrics, penned by Mercury himself, add an extra layer of intensity to this iconic piece.

The song Alaska's Flag, penned by Marie Drake, has been a part of America's musical tapestry since its publication at the start of 1935. Written in English, this notable piece captures the essence and symbolism associated with the Alaskan state flag.

Johann Sebastian Bach composed the piece *Fürchte dich nicht*, which features the poignant lyrics written by Paul Gerhardt. As you might expect from these two great artists, the song unfolds in the German language, weaving together Bach's musical genius with Gerhardt's lyrical depth to create a timeless masterpiece.
